[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Marion is the probable identification of the bride in the 1681 banns with [[Glasgow-1026|William Glasgow]], 69% for the combined couple identity. She is the possible mother of [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]], 54%, inferred from the 1682 father-only child record. A completed wedding and maternity are not directly established.
'''Marion Glasgow''' was born in 1655, recorded as a daughter of William Glasgow; the earlier biography links [[Glasgow-1556|William Glasgow]], while the current structured father is [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]]. They are separate public profiles; neither father-profile identification is established by this entry alone.<ref name="Baptism 1655">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-H5K : 16 September 2021), William Glasgow in entry for Marion Glasgow, 1655.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Kirknewton household review, 20 October 2026 ===

The fresh public WikiTree capture marks Ann McCook’s motherhood confident(flag 20). The local review explicitly downgrades that inherited certainty to an unselected uncertain alternative: the child sources cited for it name only William. This is a reassessment of a tree flag, not proof that Ann could not be Bessie’s mother; no live flag or relationship is changed. William’s existing confident father role for Bessie is individually rated 98%, without counting it as new certainty.

Findmypast’s transcript names William Glasgow and Marion Glasgow in banns dated 10 June 1681 at Kirknewton and East Calder, OPR 689/20, item 1, p.39. It gives marriage year 1681, without a separate wedding date, ages, parents, occupations or residence within the parish. This transcript was inspected on 20 October 2026. Marion’s existing findings already contained the same couple/date from the supplied ScotlandsPeople index, OPR 690/10/82, FR51; these are derivatives of one event, not independent corroboration. The original remains uninspected and the archive-reference discrepancy unresolved.

Select William Glasgow-1026 and Marion Glasgow-3025 as the probable intended couple of the 1681 banns, at 69% subjective confidence for the combined profile identification. William’s record-defined Kirknewton father account is established by Bessie’s 21 April 1682 baptism, about ten months later. The same uncommon full paternal name, parish and close sequence favour identifying that father with the groom. Marion-3025 is the existing local child account indexed in 1655, whose name, parish and ordinary mid-twenties adult generation make her the leading bride comparison. Prefer this qualified reuse of two compatible existing accounts to leaving the recorded couple unconnected or creating another William and Marion. This selects the intended couple; it does not prove a completed wedding or a ceremony date.

Select Marion Glasgow-3025 as Bessie Glasgow-1545’s possible working mother, at 54% subjective confidence, replacing Ann McCook-217 locally while retaining Ann as an unselected alternative. The 1681 named couple followed by the same-parish William’s child in April 1682 supplies positive contemporary household evidence that Ann’s inherited attachment lacks. The mother is omitted in Bessie’s inspected indexes. The lower 54% includes the bride/profile identity, groom/father identity, completion or continuation of the union, and maternity; it is not direct record wording. This is a new preferred maternal hypothesis, not a documented maternity upgrade. Ann is not biologically disproved, and her other attached children and spouse hypothesis retain their prior status.

The alternative explanations remain: another William could be the groom or Bessie’s father; the bride could be another Marion, including the compatible Inveresk Marion-1429/Marione-3049 or Edinburgh Marion-3143 accounts. The earlier 1664 William banns item supplies another adult-couple comparison, not proof of one man’s remarriage. The older William-1087 remains a possible groom comparison if the bride is a different Marion; Marion-3025’s own William-1087 father identification is ungraded and cannot be used circularly to exclude that possibility. William-3974’s recorded 1671 childhood makes him a poor ordinary groom comparison for 1681, without validating the older man’s estimated 1660 birth. Marion’s 11 October/4 November 1655 date discrepancy is retained. Neither a shared surname nor a presumed cousin marriage proves the couple’s ancestry. The pair and maternity share identity premises and are correlated assessments, not independent proofs or mechanically multiplied probabilities. William’s John-3610 father remains 24%; no mother is transferred to his later children, no biological father is changed, and all vital fields remain unchanged.

Inspect the original 1681 banns and 1682 baptism for residence, witnesses, maternal wording and any marriage completion note; reconcile both providers’ register references. Test the 1664 groom separately and compare the other Marion households. Seek an independent William/Ann record for the retained alternative.

Compared accounts: [[Glasgow-1026|Glasgow-1026]]; [[Glasgow-3025|Glasgow-3025]]; [[Glasgow-1545|Glasgow-1545]]; [[McCook-217|McCook-217]]; [[Glasgow-1087|Glasgow-1087]]; [[Glasgow-3974|Glasgow-3974]]; [[Glasgow-1429|Glasgow-1429]]; [[Glasgow-3049|Glasgow-3049]]; [[Glasgow-3143|Glasgow-3143]]; [[Glasgow-3610|Glasgow-3610]].<ref name="KirknewtonCoupleReview 2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FMAR%2F1434226%2F1&tab=this Findmypast, William Glasgow and Marion Glasgow, banns 10 June 1681; OPR689/20 item 1 p 39; transcript inspected 20 October 2026]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-H5K FamilySearch VQ4K-H5K, Marion Glasgow, indexed 1655, father William; held citation reused, conflicting indexed dates retained]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN FamilySearch VQ4K-ZQN, Bessie 1682, named father William only; held inspected citation reused]. Provider transcripts/held indexes; no original register inspection.</ref>


An Old Parish Register index records Marion Glasgow and William Glasgow at Kirknewton and East Calder on 10 June 1681.<ref name="Marriage1681">Scotland's People, ''Old Parish Registers: banns and marriages'', index entry for William Glasgow and Marion Glasgow, 10 June 1681, Kirknewton and East Calder, parish 690, reference 10/82, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Scotland’s People] (original image not inspected; supplied reciprocal index entries, reviewed 10 September 2026).</ref> The entry is compatible with this Marion by name, district and age. It does not identify either person's parents or residence, and the combined banns/marriages index cannot prove that 10 June was the wedding date. The original register is needed before attaching the recorded William as a structured spouse.

=== Supplied parish index comparison ===

The supplied Scotland’s People index records '''MARION GLASGOW''' on '''04/11/1655''' at Kirknewton and East Calder, with parent text “WILLIAM GLASGOW/”.<ref name="OPRBirth097">Scotland’s People, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms], exact surname Glasgow through 1700, index text supplied 10 September 2026: MARION GLASGOW, 04/11/1655, WILLIAM GLASGOW/, indexed gender F, Kirknewton and East Calder, parish 690, reference 10 / 37. Original register image not inspected for this review.</ref>

The profile’s structured birth date is 1655-10-11, whereas this index date is 1655-11-04. The two dates remain unreconciled. The combined births and baptisms collection does not establish whether the indexed date is a birthday or a baptism date. A parent’s name alone does not uniquely identify an attached historical person, and the index does not establish an unnamed parent. This date comparison does not resolve the possible later marriage identity discussed above.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Marion Glasgow and John Gray on 30 September 1686 at Carriden.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 664/10 / 109; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Marion Glasgow with John Bruce, smith, on 4 July 1684.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 251; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 96; PDF pp.277 and 106; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=106 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.
